This presentation needs based on my review of cyber threats, challenges, and ways to improve cyber-resilience in the energy sector. Today, energy systems use technologies such as smart treats, S. C. A. D. A, renewable energy system, and automated control. These technologies make energy systems better and more efficient, but they also create new cyber-resilience. So, this review looked at how energy systems can protect themselves, detect attacks, continue working during an attack, and prefer afterwards. Today, the energy sector is not only visible system. It is also invited to many digital systems, smart treats, S. C. A. D. A. D. A. Renewable energy, energy storage, and automated control system are all connected than share information. This makes the energy system more efficient, but it also increases the number of places that a tower can tower. For example, a tower could change a measurement send a harmful command or stop communication between. This could affect the visible operation of the energy system. This is why cyber-resilience is important. Cyber-servating mainly tries to prevent attack, but resilience also prepares the system for when an attack happens. The main idea is to anticipate, resist, detect, adapt, and recover. The review focuses on electricity system, smart treats, cyber-visceral power system, and distributed energy resources. The main question is, how can modern energy system prepare for handle, detect, and recover from cyber attacks? There are four main objectives. First, to study how cyber threats and weaknesses in the energy system have changed over time. Seven days to study different ways of protecting and recovering energy systems for cyber attacks. Third days to identify the main research trends and the current problem more gaps in this area. And fourth one is to identify future research areas that can make energy system more secure and more resilient. For this review, a Christmas-based process was used to organize the literature review. First is identification. 11 research papers were searched using suitable keywords and economic resources. Seven days is training, duplicate papers and papers that were not relevant were removed. Third is eligibility. The remaining papers were checked using the inclusion and exclusion criteria. Finally, the selected papers were studies and compared to find the main research teams and findings. The review mainly focuses on research about smart treats, cyber-visceral power systems, distributed energy resources, micro-drites, and cyber-resiliences. The cyber security rates in the energy sector have changed over time. In the beginning, the main focus was a traditional IT system and a CADA system. Then smart treats technologies became more common. More sensors, devices, and communication systems were targeted to the grid. This created a much larger attack surface. Later, we started seeing attacks that could affect the visible operation of the power system. The Ukraine-Power Red attack in is an important example. Today, we also have distributed energy resources, renewable energy, and micro-drites. Because of these changes, research is moving from simply protect system to making the whole energy system more resilient. There are several major cyber threats to energy system. First is false data injection. We are attacked. We are attacked. We have changed data measurement to make the system made the front decision. Seven days. Then some were in Malvea, which can stop system from working properly. Third is Daniela Service-Set-H, which can make communication or service unavailable. Another threat is credential from Promise. We are attacked. There are also supply chain attacks. We are weaknesses in software, hardware, vendors, or other connected components are used. Finally, cyber attacks can cause cascading failures. We are a problem in one part of the system can affect other parts. The research shows that we cannot depend on only one security method. First is prevention. This includes security system design, access control, and different layers of security. Seven days detection. The system needs to quickly identify unusual activities, so attacks that don't need mitigation. Once an attack is found, its impact need to be reduced. Both this adaptation. The system should be able to change its response when the attack or system condition changes. Finally, the ice recovery. The system needs to safely restore normal operation after an attack, so the main idea is that even if prevention fails, the system should still be able to continue important operation and recovery. When we look at the research together, we can see several important trends. First, researchers are moving towards protecting the whole cyber-PCRAL energy system, not just the IT site. Seven, AI draft-based method are performing more important for detecting attacks and understanding what is happening in the system. Third one is renewable energy distributed, energy resources, and micro-drives are creating a new security and resilience problem. However, there are still some gaps. There are not enough common ways to measure cyber-resilience. Many solutions are still tested mainly using simulations. Security system also needs to become more flexible when it has changed, and IT recovery and not recovery are not always properly connected. Based on these research gaps, the review identifies few future research areas. First, resilient metrics. We need better ways to measure how well and energy system can continue working and recovery after cyber attack. Seven, one is adaptive cyber defense. Future security system should be able to change their response when the attack or change their methods. The digital to Indian test bits. This can help researchers test cyber attacks and defense methods in more realistic energy system environment. For Thunnees, resilience by design. Resilience should be included from the beginning when design renewable system, micro-drives, and distributed energy system. Finally, integrated IT and OT recovery. Future recovery plans should consider both the technical system and the people who operate them. The conclusion is, the energy sector is becoming more digital, more connected, and more decentralized. This gives us many benefits, but it also increased the possible impact of cyber attacks the research shows that cyber severity alone is not enough. Energy system need to be able to protect data, adapt, and recovery. This means security should be included when the energy system is designed and not added only after a problem happens. The main message from this review is that cyber resilience needs to work together. A strong energy system should be prepared not only to prevent attack, but also to continue operating and recovery when attacks happen. These are some of the main references used for this review. The complete references list is included in the review paper using the IEEE format. This studies how a smart grid security cyber visible attacks distributed energy resources, cyber resilience, and attack detection. Thank you for listening.
